title: I made a Tetris zombie survival game with CODEX
author: SheepherderPure4141
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I wanted to test whether I could turn a real-world 3D Gaussian Splatting scene into a playable game with ChatGPT/Codex helping with development.

Somehow, it became a zombie survival game with Tetris.

You move around the map collecting pieces, which drop into a Tetris board on the left. Clearing lines earns weapon XP. Better weapons help you survive the next zombie wave, and later upgrades let you combine different bullet effects.

Most of the development loop was me playing it, finding something annoying, and asking AI to change it. Then playing again and finding something else.

Chairs kept trapping the player. Zombies got stuck on stairs. Weapons became so powerful that the late game was easier than the beginning. Getting those things right took a lot of back and forth.

Here’s the demo:  
[https://demo-blood-moon.xgrids.com/](https://demo-blood-moon.xgrids.com/)

Desktop + keyboard recommended.

I’ve played it enough that I probably can’t judge it objectively anymore. If you give it a try, I’d like to know whether the Tetris/survival combination actually works—and where it starts feeling boring or unfair.

Also happy to share more about the AI development process if anyone’s interested.
